findings.title: `raw_counts` has no product filter: cross-product `tick_trade` rows will read as false mismatches
findings.description: `raw_counts` counts every `tick_trade` row whose `ts_event` falls inside one of the product's session intervals — no restriction to the product's instruments or units — while the other side of the proof, `ledger_totals`, is shape-filtered through `_SHAPE_WHERE` (`dataset`, `symbols`, `stype_in`, tier schemas, `COVERAGE_PREDICATE`). Today the universe holds only ES and every ingested unit is of the `ES.FUT`/`PARENT` shape, so the two sides agree and the new tests pass. But `universe.py` and `constants.py` both state GC joins in slice 231, and CME metals sessions largely overlap equity sessions: once GC units are ingested into the shared `tick_trade` table, `mt data tick coverage --product ES` will count GC trades inside ES session intervals. `_session_row` in `tick_coverage.py` unions instruments from `ledger` *and* `raw`, so every raw-only GC instrument becomes `Mismatch(ledger=0, raw=N)` by construction, and the CLI exits 3 — accusing an operator of an out-of-band edit on every overlapping session (symmetrically for `--product GC`). The raw side of a per-product proof needs to be restricted to the product's instruments (join the row's unit to the shape, or filter `instrument_id` against the shape's definitions), or 231 will inherit a proof that cannot pass.

findings.title: No load-tier test for the new status/coverage read paths
findings.description: Slice 225's load tier covers only ingest (`test_225_tick_ingest_nfr.py`; 224 has `test_224_tick_pass_nfr.py`). The read verbs introduced here include the slice's heaviest new query: `raw_counts` scans every `tick_trade` row in `[min(open), max(close)]` and joins it against an `unnest` array of sessions — a nested loop whose cost grows with both range size and session count — plus the manifest/ledger/definition scans in `shape_units`, `ledger_totals` and `contract_lines`. The integration tests exercise two-day ranges under the 30 s pytest timeout; nothing asserts a realistic configuration (a month, or the full ingested span) completes within a latency bound. Per the project's Python rules (load-test tier for environment-layer paths, gating on latency/resource bounds) and the tier's own precedent for this initiative, add a load test gating `coverage` — and ideally `status` — on a realistic range.

findings.title: `build_status` reads the unit manifest twice per product
findings.description: `_product_status` awaits `_scope(...)`, which calls `shape_units(conn, shape_of(entry))`, and then passes the scoped sessions into `session_verdicts(...)`, which awaits `shape_units` again with identical arguments. On the autocommit connection from `connect_migrated` these are two separate statements — two snapshots: a unit committed between them changes the verdict of a day already scoped. Harmless for today's single-product CLI read (one extra manifest query), but passing the units through (or scoping inside `session_verdicts`) would make the scope and the verdicts observe one state and halve the manifest reads.

findings.title: `READ_EPILOG` under-describes exit 4
findings.description: The epilog says exit 4 means "the tick or production (calendar) database is unreachable", but `calendar_sessions` in `tick_status_build.py` also wraps `OutOfPopulatedRangeError` into `TickCalendarError`, which `exit_code_for` maps to `EXIT_STORAGE`. So `coverage --end` beyond the calendar's populated span exits 4 while both databases are reachable and answering. The error text itself names the remedy (`mt data extend`), but the epilog's stated contract for the code is narrower than the behavior; widen the wording (compare `INGEST_EPILOG`'s generic "storage (tick database or calendar)").

findings.title: Coverage's "raw rows change only through supersession or by hand" premise is untested for reopened/reset units
findings.description: The module docstring grounds the exit-3 semantics on raw rows changing only via supersession (whose ledger `COVERAGE_PREDICATE` excludes) or manual edits. Supersession is covered — `test_tick_status_reads.py` proves superseded units are excluded from both reads, and `test_tick_status_build.py` proves a deleted row mismatches — but nothing exercises coverage after a unit is *reopened* or *reset*. A reopened unit is excluded from the ledger by the same predicate, and I could not verify in this review (I did not read `reset.py` or `manifest_transitions.py`) whether resetting an already-ingested unit also deletes its `tick_trade` rows; if it does not, `coverage` would report that unit's rows as raw-only mismatches. Add a test that resets/reopens an ingested unit and asserts coverage stays ok, or document the invariant `reset` must maintain.

structured_findings.summary: `raw_counts` has no product filter: cross-product `tick_trade` rows will read as false mismatches
No load-tier test for the new status/coverage read paths
`build_status` reads the unit manifest twice per product
Coverage's "raw rows change only through supersession or by hand" premise is untested for reopened/reset units
